Resume a saved session

How to Resume the Right Codex CLI Session

Use codex resume to pick a saved interactive session, or codex resume SESSION_ID when you already have its ID. --last looks in the current working directory. Add --all to search across directories. For scripts, use codex exec resume and verify the returned thread ID before continuing.

  1. Choose how to find the session
  2. Resume by ID
  3. Resume the latest in a folder
  4. Find a missing session
  5. See the actual session selections

Which Codex session do you need?

See stepsSee stepsSee steps

Resume a known session ID

In a terminal, switch to the project directory and replace SESSION_ID with the saved ID:

codex resume SESSION_ID

The interactive CLI can ask which directory to use if it differs from the saved session. Pick the intended checkout. For a non-interactive continuation, pass the ID and a new prompt:

codex exec --json resume SESSION_ID "Summarize where we left off without editing files." > resumed.jsonl

In resumed.jsonl, find the thread.started event and compare its thread_id with the ID you intended. For a scripted check with jq:

jq -r 'select(.type == "thread.started") | .thread_id' resumed.jsonl

To start a second conversation or use a separate checkout, see Codex forks and worktrees.

Use the Codex exec JSONL guide for full turn and reply checks.

Check the command’s exit status and the working directory as well. The session ID identifies the conversation. It does not verify the current Git branch, file contents or permissions.

Continue the latest session in the current directory

codex resume --last

Run this from the checkout where you used the CLI. If you want to choose among other folders, start with codex resume --all and inspect the directory in the picker. Adding --last as well lets Codex choose across folders, so use an exact ID when you need a particular session.

A non-interactive follow-up uses codex exec resume --last "your prompt". In our Codex 0.172.0 test, running that command from a directory without a saved session started a new thread and exited successfully. If you depend on saved context, verify the returned ID.

Find a session missing from the CLI picker

  1. Check the working directory. A project clone and another worktree have different paths. In interactive Codex, use codex resume --all to inspect sessions across paths.
  2. Check how you ran it. Use codex resume --include-non-interactive to include non-interactive runs in the picker on releases that support this flag. Check codex resume --help on your machine.
  3. Check which history was saved. codex exec --ephemeral runs without saving a resumable local session. If you use a separate CLI profile or machine, open the environment where you saved the session.

If a resumed run begins with a fresh ID, stop and verify the intended history before sending additional work. If you only have an exported JSONL file, keep it private. It may contain prompts, paths or tool output. The local Codex log reader covers token counters separately.

What the CLI selected in two test directories

We created synthetic sessions in two disposable Git directories and ran the non-interactive CLI against a loopback endpoint that returned a fixed string. The selection check used real CLI events and locally saved fixture records. It covers the CLI’s behavior and does not measure model recall.

Codex CLI 0.172.0 · commands issued from test project A unless noted
CheckThread selectedRecorded working directory
exec resume --lastA’s saved threadA
exec resume --last --allNewest thread in BB
exec resume with the older B IDOlder thread in BB
exec resume --last in a folder with no saved threadNew threadThat folder

The temporary --ephemeral run produced a thread ID but no saved session file. Resuming that exact ID failed before any model request. Download the tested IDs, exit codes and recorded working directories. The interactive picker and directory prompt are documented behavior.

Follow the current interactive resume reference or the non-interactive guide. Check whether your installed release supports the options you plan to use.

For project rules missing after a fresh launch, check which AGENTS.md files Codex loads.
